title: Why Evolution Is True
author: Jerry A. Coyne
target_audience: General readers interested in science and evolution
Students studying biology or related fields
Teachers and educators seeking accessible resources on evolution
Individuals skeptical about evolution or seeking evidence-based explanations
Non-scientists looking for a clear introduction to evolutionary theory
core_themes: Mechanisms of evolution (natural selection, genetic drift, speciation)
Genetics and molecular biology support for evolution
primary_purpose: To concisely articulate the overwhelming scientific evidence supporting evolution, clarify misconceptions, and explain why the theory remains the best explanation for the diversity of life on Earth.

structure_format.narrative_style: Clear, authoritative, and engaging scientific prose
structure_format.organization: Thematic chapters covering foundational concepts and evidentiary lines (fossil record, biogeography, embryology, genetics, etc.)
features: Examples and case studies from the natural world
Clear explanations of complex scientific ideas

key_concepts_lessons: Evolution is supported by multiple, independent lines of scientific evidence.
Natural selection is a powerful and observable mechanism driving evolutionary change.
Transitional fossils and genetic data document the gradual modification of species over time.
Common ancestry links all living organisms, as shown by anatomical, embryological, and molecular similarities.
Misconceptions and misunderstandings about evolution often stem from misinformation or lack of scientific literacy.
The diversity and complexity of life on Earth are best explained by evolutionary processes, not by supernatural intervention.
style_tone: Respectful yet forthright when addressing antievolution arguments
notable_features: Synthesizes vast scientific evidence into accessible language
Extensive use of real-world examples (e.g., stickleback fish, Darwin's finches)
Includes up-to-date (as of publication) research findings
cultural_historical_context: Written during ongoing public debates over evolution, especially in the United States, 'Why Evolution Is True' responds to persistent challenges by creationism and intelligent design, aiming to reaffirm the scientific consensus on evolution for a broad audience.
reception_impact: Well-received by scientists, educators, and the general public for its clarity and thoroughness
Praised for making complex science approachable without sacrificing rigor
Used in classrooms and recommended as an introduction to evolution
Occasionally criticized by creationist and ID advocates for its strong stance
comparable_titles: The Greatest Show on Earth by Richard Dawkins
Your Inner Fish by Neil Shubin
Why Darwin Matters by Michael Shermer
The Blind Watchmaker by Richard Dawkins
